es: Escribir réplicas que sugieren sin afirmar: rechazar una invitación, criticar con tacto, pedir que te lleven y cerrar con una aclaración.

teaching.en: Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to, but I might have other plans that evening, so I may have to decline.
teaching.es: ¡Gracias por la invitación! Me encantaría, pero puede que tenga otros planes esa tarde, así que quizá tenga que rechazarla.
teaching.explanationEs: Agradecer, desear y poner una pega: el rechazo queda implícito en might have other plans.
segments: Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to, but I might have
other plans that evening, so I may have to decline.
teaching.audioText: Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to, but I might have other plans that evening, so I may have to decline.

teaching.en: If you want to let someone down gently, stay tactful and noncommittal: 'I'm not sure I can make it' is kinder than a flat no.
teaching.es: Si quieres rechazar a alguien con delicadeza, sé diplomático y evasivo: «No estoy seguro de poder ir» es más amable que un no rotundo.
teaching.explanationEs: Tactful es cuidar los sentimientos del otro; noncommittal es no comprometerse con una respuesta clara.
segments: If you want to let someone down gently, stay tactful and noncommittal: 'I'm
not sure I can make it' is kinder than a flat no.
teaching.audioText: If you want to let someone down gently, stay tactful and noncommittal: 'I'm not sure I can make it' is kinder than a flat no.

teaching.en: Some people beat around the bush for minutes before admitting that the soup is too salty, and the pause says more than the words.
teaching.es: Hay quien se anda por las ramas durante minutos antes de admitir que la sopa está demasiado salada, y la pausa dice más que las palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: Beat around the bush es evitar ir al grano; aquí la pausa ya comunica la crítica.
segments: Some people beat around the bush for minutes before admitting that the
soup is too salty, and the pause says more than the words.
teaching.audioText: Some people beat around the bush for minutes before admitting that the soup is too salty, and the pause says more than the words.

teaching.en: The soup is... interesting. Is it a new recipe? That polite pause can tell the cook what you think without a direct criticism.
teaching.es: La sopa es... interesante. ¿Es una receta nueva? Esa pausa cortés puede decirle al cocinero lo que piensas sin criticarlo directamente.
teaching.explanationEs: Interesting con pausa y pregunta evita decir «no me gusta»: la crítica se deduce.
segments: The soup is... interesting. Is it a new recipe? That polite pause
can tell the cook what you think without a direct criticism.
teaching.audioText: The soup is... interesting. Is it a new recipe? That polite pause can tell the cook what you think without a direct criticism.

teaching.en: It's quite a long way home, isn't it? I could use a ride, since the last bus has already left.
teaching.es: Es un camino bastante largo a casa, ¿no? Me vendría bien que me llevaran, ya que el último autobús se ha ido.
teaching.explanationEs: Observación + coletilla: la petición de ride queda sugerida sin formularla.
segments: It's quite a long way home, isn't it? I could
use a ride, since the last bus has already left.
teaching.audioText: It's quite a long way home, isn't it? I could use a ride, since the last bus has already left.

teaching.en: Let me clarify: I did like the soup, but I'm busy on Saturday, so please don't think that I'm being distant.
teaching.es: Déjame aclarar: la sopa sí me gustó, pero el sábado estoy ocupado, así que por favor no pienses que me estoy mostrando distante.
teaching.explanationEs: Clarify cierra la conversación corrigiendo una posible mala interpretación de lo insinuado.
segments: Let me clarify: I did like the soup, but I'm busy
on Saturday, so please don't think that I'm being distant.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que rechaza con tacto la invitación al cine.

choices.text: Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to, and I'm sure I'll be free that evening.
No, thanks. Films are boring, and I never have plans on Fridays.
Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to, but I might have plans that evening.

feedback.es: Agradecer, expresar deseo y dejar una pega abierta rechaza sin ofender; las otras dos aceptan o rechazan sin ningún tacto.

hint.es: Busca agradecimiento, deseo y una excusa abierta, sin un no rotundo.

origin.text: Mia invites you to the cinema on Friday. You do not want to go, but you do not want to upset her either.

prompt.es: Completa: «No sé si puedo ir. Puede que tenga planes con mi familia.»

feedback.es: Might have plans deja el rechazo implícito y no compromete a quien habla: el otro debe deducirlo.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo plural que significa «planes».

origin.text: I'm not sure that I can come. I might have ___ with my family that evening, so I can't promise anything.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es un camino bastante largo a casa, ¿no?»

answer.text: It is quite a long way home isn't it

feedback.es: Home es adverbio y no lleva to; la coletilla isn't it convierte la observación en una sugerencia que pide confirmar.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué logra la narradora con «it's… interesting».

choices.text: She hints that she dislikes it without hurting her friend.
She shows that she loved it and wants a second bowl.
She asks for the recipe because she wants to try it at home.

feedback.es: La pausa y la pregunta Is it new? critican la sopa sin decirlo; la amiga lo entiende y confirma que tenía demasiada sal.

origin.audio: After the dinner, my friend asked me what I thought of her new recipe. I tried the soup and said, Hmm, it's... interesting. Is it new? She smiled, because she knew exactly what I meant. Then she tasted it herself and laughed, admitting that she had made it far too salty. I had avoided hurting her feelings, and she had saved me from having to say that it was salty.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es un camino largo a casa, ¿no? Me vendría bien que me lleven.»

feedback.es: I could use a ride es la forma indirecta de pedir que te lleven a casa; lift es la variante británica.

origin.text: It's a long way home, isn't it? It's getting late, and I could use a ___.

prompt.es: Elige la frase con la que el jefe frena con tacto a un compañero.

choices.text: That's a great story. Keep talking, we have enough time.
That's a great story. Let's hear what the others think, shall we?
Stop talking now. Nobody wants to hear your stories.

feedback.es: Elogiar la historia y ceder la palabra a los demás es una indirecta cortés: frena al compañero sin humillarlo.

origin.text: A colleague keeps interrupting the meeting with long stories. The manager wants him to stop, without making him look bad in front of the team.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué intención tiene Tom con sus respuestas.

choices.text: To show that he is annoyed with his sister about something.
To ask his sister for time to check his diary.
To avoid accepting without openly saying no.

feedback.es: Tom agradece, pone una pega vaga y cambia de tema: evita aceptar sin tener que decir un no abierto a su hermana.

origin.audio: Tom's sister invited him to a party on Saturday. He thanked her warmly and said, I'd love to, but I might have other plans. When she asked what plans, he answered, Oh, nothing I can really talk about yet. Then he quickly changed the subject to her new flat.

prompt.es: Lee la nota. ¿Qué hace el autor con «It's... different»?

choices.text: He criticises the jumper tactfully while thanking her.
He thanks her warmly and says that he loves the jumper.
He apologises because the jumper does not fit him.

feedback.es: It's... different con pausa evita elogiar de verdad; el agradecimiento por el detalle mantiene el tono amable y deja la crítica implícita.

origin.text: Dear Aunt Rosa, thank you so much for the jumper. It's... different, and I can see that you chose it with great care. It was very kind of you to think of me.

prompt.es: Completa: «Gracias por preguntar, pero preferiría no ir.»

feedback.es: I'd rather not es la fórmula educada para rechazar; «I prefer no» sería un calco del español.

origin.text: Thank you for asking, but I'd ___ not. I have a lot to do this week, and I wouldn't be good company.

prompt.es: Escribe tu chat con Mia: cinco indirectas y una aclaración final.

answer.text: Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to, but I might have other plans on Saturday, so I'm not sure that I can come. The soup is... interesting. Is it a new recipe? It's getting late, isn't it? Some of us have classes tomorrow. Some people are always a bit late, aren't they? It's quite a long way home, isn't it? I could use a ride. Let me clarify: the soup is a bit salty, but I'm not angry, and I'd rather not promise anything about Saturday, because my weekend is busy. I hope you understand, and thanks again for asking me, because it really was a lovely idea.
accepted: Thanks for the invitation! I'd love to, but I might have other plans on Saturday, so I'm not sure that I can come. The soup is... interesting. Is it a new recipe? It's getting late, isn't it? Some of us have classes tomorrow. Some people are always a bit late, aren't they? It's quite a long way home, isn't it? I could use a ride. Let me clarify: the soup is a bit salty, but I'm not angry, and I'd rather not promise anything about Saturday, because my weekend is busy. I hope you understand, and thanks again for asking me, because it really was a lovely idea.

Thank you for the invitation! I'd love to, but I think I have other plans on Saturday, and I can't promise anything. The soup is interesting. Is it a new recipe? It's quite late, isn't it? I have an early class tomorrow. Some people are never on time, aren't they? It's a long way home, isn't it? I could use a lift. Let me clarify: I liked the soup, although it was a bit salty, and I'm not angry at all. I'd rather not say yes to Saturday yet, because my weekend is busy. Thanks for understanding, and sorry if I sounded distant.

Thanks for the invitation! I would love to, but I might have other plans that evening. Hmm, this soup is interesting. Is it a new recipe? We should go soon, shouldn't we? Some people are always late, aren't they? It's a long way home, isn't it? I could use a ride. Let me clarify: I loved the company, and the soup is a bit salty, but I'm not upset. I'd rather not promise about Saturday yet, because I'm busy that weekend. I hope you don't mind, and thanks again for asking.

feedback.es: El chat mantiene cinco indirectas (agradecer con pega, criticar con pausa, sugerir con una tag, reprochar con tacto y pedir un ride) y cierra con una aclaración.

origin.text: Chatea con Mia en inglés (140–190 palabras). Escribe cinco réplicas con una indirecta cada una, sin decir «no» ni «quiero», y una aclaración final: 1) te invita a una fiesta el sábado y no quieres ir; 2) te pregunta si te gusta su sopa, que está salada; 3) es muy tarde y quieres irte (usa una question tag); 4) una amiga llega siempre tarde y quieres reprochárselo con tacto (usa una question tag); 5) necesitas que te lleven a casa (usa una question tag); 6) aclara al final qué querías decir.

prompt.es: Lee el correo. ¿Qué da a entender la autora con «an ambitious start»?

choices.text: That the draft is too ambitious and needs to be shorter.
That the draft has real problems, which she mentions gently.
That she is enthusiastic and wants to publish it as it is.

feedback.es: An ambitious start y I wonder whether suavizan una crítica real: el final y el principio necesitan trabajo, pero se dice con tacto.

origin.text: Hi Carlos, thanks for the draft. I've read it twice and, honestly, it's an ambitious start. I wonder whether the ending might need a little more work, and perhaps the opening too. Shall we go through it together on Friday?

prompt.es: Completa: «Me temo que tendré que rechazar tu amable invitación.»

feedback.es: Decline es el verbo formal para rechazar una invitación con cortesía; el motivo del evento familiar lo hace más amable.

origin.text: I'm afraid I'll have to ___ your kind invitation, because I have a family event that weekend.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Preferiría no prometer nada sobre el sábado todavía.»

answer.text: I'd rather not promise anything about Saturday yet

feedback.es: I'd rather not evita un no directo y yet deja la puerta abierta para decidir más adelante.
